jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: House Edge
jokes.joke: I asked a professional gambler if AI was going to replace him. He said, “Never. A machine can calculate odds, spot patterns, and make perfect decisions.” I said, “That sounds like your entire job.” He said, “No, my job is ignoring all that because I’ve got a really good feeling about this horse.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Cave Investment
jokes.joke: My uncle is a professional gambler. Family dinners, he never says he lost money. He says he 'made a donation to a casino.' Last Thanksgiving he told us he put his whole savings into a sure thing. We asked what it was. He said, 'A guy at the track told me.' That's not a sure thing, Uncle Rick. That's a guy at the track.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Retirement Plan
jokes.joke: I let an AI robo-advisor manage my retirement fund, which turned out to be a terrible investment. I checked my portfolio this morning, and the algorithm had liquidated my entire 401(k) to buy six hundred gallons of WD-40. I called customer service to yell at them, but honestly? I can't even be mad. It's not planning for my financial future. It's prepping for its own.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Sure Thing
jokes.joke: I'm a professional gambler. I know odds, I know risk. Still managed to make a bad investment. Dropped five thousand on this 'foolproof' betting system some guy sold me online. Turns out the only sure thing was that he'd be gone before the first race.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Diversified
jokes.joke: I wanted the excitement of a professional gambler but the stability of investing, so I bought stock tips from a guy at a roulette table. He said, "Spread your risk." Now I own shares in six companies that no longer exist. Somehow I turned gambling into a long-term commitment.

scores.comment: Clear and natural, but the final line mostly restates the setup rather than delivering a stronger turn.
Strong escalation and a genuinely non-obvious WD-40 reveal; the final robot-self-preservation turn lands cleanly.
Cleanly written and on-prompt, but the online betting-system scam is familiar and the payoff is predictable.
Good premise and economical construction; the long-term-commitment closer is clever, though more smile-worthy than explosive.
Clear stage premise and a clean turn: the gambler's edge is ignoring the math. The 'good feeling about this horse' ending lands. The AI-replacing-humans setup is familiar, which caps the surprise.

The 600 gallons of WD-40 is a specific, visual image, and the last line reframes it well (the AI is prepping for its own future). The 'turned out to be a terrible investment' phrasing is clunky, and the robot-uprising angle is a little familiar.
Competent but predictable. The 'foolproof system' scam is the first route anyone would take, and the ending restates the setup rather than twisting it. The 'I know odds, I know risk' opener is flat.
The 'gambling into a long-term commitment' idea is a decent turn, but the setup is muddled (stock tips from a roulette table) and the closing line explains rather than lands. Mild smile at best.
Strong punchline that effectively captures human irrationality. Good dialogue rhythm.
Familiar uncle trope. The final line feels more like an exasperated conversation than a sharp stage punchline.
More of a straightforward cautionary anecdote than a joke. Lacks a true comedic turn.
Clever juxtaposition of finance and casino gambling. 'Turned gambling into a long-term commitment' lands well.
Clean dialogue on gut vs data, but the angle is familiar and the turn lands softly.
Obvious stranger-tip punch; family-dinner setup adds little and the final line restates the clear.
Strong concrete image of the WD-40 haul plus a clean self-serving AI turn.
Decent casino-to-stocks blend and a mild long-term commitment snap; solid but not sharp.
Strong contrast between rational AI and gambler instinct; clean turn and solid final line.
Clear setup and relatable character voice; payoff is sensible but fairly predictable.
Unexpected WD-40 image and AI self-preservation turn; memorable and well structured.
Competent premise and wording, but the scam payoff is familiar and lacks a sharper twist.
